newsitem.title: FRANCE: Eramet to review mining assets swap.
newsitem.headline: Eramet to review mining assets swap.

text.p: French nickel producer Eramet said on Tuesday it would review a proposal to reallocate mining reserves in New Caledonia.
The plan, which entails the exchange of nickel mines, would allow another group to build a nickel plant in the north of the French territory.

"Eramet confirms it is ready to review the terms of an agreement to swap, on fair basis, the mining titles of the Koniambo field belonging to SLN with those of the Poum field," Eramet said in a statement.
Societe Le Nickel (SLN) is the company that oversees all Eramet's holdings in New Caledonia.
Between October 22 and October 24 the French government headed talks over the future of mining reserves in the Pacific territory.
In a statement released earlier in the day, the Overseas Territories Ministry said the talks led to a proposal to swap the Poum and Koniambo mining assets.
Mining resources from the Koniambo field would be used to supply a nickel plant to be build in the north of the territory by Canadian group Falconbridge and by the SMSP company.
The proposal must be agreed by the boards of the companies involved in the swap.

Under a 1988 plan to ease separatists' tensions in New Caledonia, France has agreed to help rebalance the interest of local Kanak people against those of French settlers ahead of a vote on independence set for 1998.
As part of the plan, France supports a project by the pro-independence Kanak Socialist Liberation Front (FLNKS) and Falconbridge to build a nickel plant in the north of New Caledonia.
Eramet Chairman Yves Rambaud said in early October he was not against the new plant as long as it did not threaten the development of Eramet in New Caledonia.
